newsitem.title: USA: Ryder says capital spending below outlook.
newsitem.headline: Ryder says capital spending below outlook.

text.p: Ryder System Inc Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Anthony Burns said the company's capital spending for 1996 is at a rate below its full year target of $1.5 billion versus $1.7 billion last year.
"We have spent around $700 million in first three quarters," Burns said during a conference call following release of the company's third quarter financial results.
"Our estimate right now is in the neighborhood of $1.4 billion, or slightly above $1.4 billion," he said of the full year capital spending outlook.

Reducing capital spending levels and keeping them lower over the next few years is one of Ryder's major goals, noted Burns. The company also is refocusing its businesses to focus on long-term contractual activities including its integrated logistics business and restructuring, including cutting some employees.

Ryder said it plans to announce a major restructuring charge, in the range of $75 to $150 million in the fourth quarter. "Most of the improvement should become more evident in the first quarter of 1997," he told the conference call.
The company also had announced a program to buy back up to six million shares of its stock, following the sale of its consumer truck rental business, which was completed on October 17.
"Cash has been received and we're starting to pay down debt," Ryder Chief Financial Officer Edwin Huston told the conference call.
Burns said the share buyback program would be on the open market and would begin soon. "We would anticipate that we would conclude it within three to four months," he said.
